parts.note: so can mean 'thereupon' or 'and then', as in 'so he left'
to spike a drink is to lace it with alcohol or a drug

explanation.surface: A spiked drink is offered as a way of easing someone's distress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spike' looks like a noun or a dog's name, but it is the verb meaning to doctor a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Comfort in grief or trouble is a form of relief.

parts.note: Tommy Atkins is the nickname for a British private soldier
on means about or concerning, as in 'a talk on birds'

explanation.surface: A British soldier is about to keep going.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy is old slang for a British army private. 'about to' looks like 'on the point of' but splits as ON plus a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry on doggedly despite difficulty is to persevere.

clue.text: Forgiving a mistake in line ten

indicators.note: a mistake in the line suggests the letters have been put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A tolerant judge overlooks an error in line ten of a text.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenient means mild and tolerant, ready to pardon.

clue.text: Unpleasant cure taken on Boxing Day?

definitions.meaning: abrupt withdrawal from an addictive drug, a harsh form of treatment
leftover roast bird eaten chilled the day after Christmas

explanation.surface: A grim remedy is administered on the day after Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: Boxing Day is the British holiday on 26 December, when leftovers from Christmas dinner are eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: abrupt drug withdrawal, and the chilled leftovers of the Christmas roast eaten next day.

parts.note: a square is a number such as 4, 9 or 16, the product of a whole number with itself
up means in residence at a university, especially Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: Someone settles a figure while living in a house, or a student pays rent.
explanation.walkthrough: UP for 'in residence' is a British usage: a student is 'up' at Oxford or Cambridge during term.
explanation.definitionFit: To square up a debt is to pay off what is owed, which is to settle it.

definitions.meaning: fit means suitably trained or competent for a job
a statement made with reservations is limited or hedged

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: competent through training, and limited by conditions, as in qualified praise.

clue.text: Girl no novice in the air

indicators.note: no means the following letter is dropped from the name

parts.note: Laura is a girl's name
L is the learner sign, so it stands for a novice

explanation.surface: A girl who is no beginner is up in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no novice' looks like a description of the girl, but it tells you to remove L.
explanation.definitionFit: An aura is a distinctive atmosphere around a person or place, so something felt in the air.

definitions.meaning: special as in a special delivery, sent by a fast dedicated service
a fast train with few stops

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: an express delivery is a special fast service, and an express is a fast train.

clue.text: Tax inspector's mean — he gets the money

parts.note: PAYE (pay as you earn) is the British system of deducting income tax from wages

indicators.note: mean here is the midpoint, so the central letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A stingy tax inspector is the one who ends up with the cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' looks like stingy but means the middle: the central (fifth) letter of 'inspector' is E.
explanation.definitionFit: The person to whom a sum is paid is its recipient.

indicators.note: hear tells us the word is to be listened to, a different spelling of the same sound

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is told to listen to a title or name.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: ANNE is an example of a name, an appellation.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name is an example of an appellation, a name or title.

clue.text: Fat — none on a pupil's back

indicators.note: back tells us to read the whole string of pieces from end to start

parts.note: nil means none or nothing
taken as written
L is the learner sign, and a pupil is a learner

explanation.surface: A remark about a pupil whose back carries no fat at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the whole run NILONAL, giving LANOLIN. 'pupil's back' looks like a body part but 'back' is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanolin is the greasy substance from sheep's wool, a kind of fat used in ointments.

parts.note: a cup is one example of a trophy, as the 'perhaps' signals

explanation.surface: A sports cup is dismissed as a waste of effort or money.
explanation.definitionFit: Atrophy is the wasting away of a body part or tissue from disuse or disease.

clue.text: One following delinquent not entirely beset by difficulties

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
next means following, as in 'the next day'

indicators.note: not entirely means the word loses its final letter, so it is cut short

parts.note: remiss means negligent of duty, a sense of delinquent

explanation.surface: A youth trailing behind a not-quite-bad friend finds himself in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' drops the last S of REMISS to leave REMIS. 'delinquent' looks like a noun for a young offender but is an adjective meaning neglectful.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means in extreme circumstances, especially at the point of death or great difficulty.

clue.text: Make much of a lot, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak tells us the word is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: one's lot is one's fate or destiny

explanation.surface: Someone is told to make a great fuss about a large quantity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot' looks like a large amount, but it is one's lot in life. In British speech fete is said like 'fate'.
explanation.definitionFit: To fete someone is to honour or celebrate them lavishly, making a great fuss of them.

indicators.note: it'll change says the letters before it are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rule once laid down is hinted to be about to change.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal maximum on driving speed is a restriction.

parts.note: re is a short word meaning about or concerning
all in is an informal phrase for exhausted

explanation.surface: Being completely exhausted, someone went to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Retired here means went to bed, which is what 'turned in' means informally.

parts.note: to deter is to discourage from acting
to sap or mine is to dig under fortifications to undermine them

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to dishearten a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sap' looks like a fool or tree juice, but it is the military verb meaning to tunnel under.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle or resolve on something is to decide it.

indicators.note: reverts means the road's letters go back the other way

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written MI in crosswords
passé is French borrowed into English for out of date

explanation.surface: A road returns to being an old-fashioned dead end.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; crosswords write it MI, so 'reverts' turns it into IM.
explanation.definitionFit: A cul-de-sac is literally a dead end, and figuratively a deadlock or position with no way forward.

indicators.note: accommodating means holding something inside, so one piece goes within another
in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to race is to hurry
7 Down is EXPRESS, and to express is to state

explanation.surface: A car with seven seats is urged to get a move on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses RACE to ECAR, which holds STATE (EXPRESS, the answer to 7, as a verb).
explanation.definitionFit: A car with a long body and rear door for carrying loads is a kind of motor vehicle.

clue.text: Jack in case that's most impressive

parts.note: in cribbage, 'his nob' is the jack of the turned-up suit, so nob can stand for jack
lest means in case or for fear that

explanation.surface: A playing card kept in a box is described as the finest thing around.
explanation.walkthrough: NOB for jack comes from cribbage, a card game, where 'one for his nob' scores for holding the jack. 'in case' looks like a container but is one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The noblest is the grandest or most magnificent, the superlative of a word for stately.

clue.text: Pet animal rests up in the garden

indicators.note: rests ... in means one piece lies within another
in shows the reversed animal goes inside the garden word

parts.note: a bed is a plot in a garden

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a vole is a small rodent

explanation.surface: A pet creature lies down in the garden for a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns VOLE into ELOV, which 'rests in' BED.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet is someone cherished, a darling or loved one.

clue.text: Steeped to produce this kind of dye

indicators.note: to produce suggests the letters are worked up into something new

explanation.surface: Cloth soaked long enough gives a particular dye.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'of the deepest dye' means of the most extreme kind; the clue reads it literally, a dye of the most intense colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The most intense shade of a dye is its darkest, most saturated colour.

clue.text: Germany's first pair are in before time, out of enthusiasm

indicators.note: are in means the letters go inside another word

parts.note: early means ahead of the appointed time

indicators.note: first pair means the opening two letters of the word are taken

explanation.surface: A German side's top two are in early, out of sheer keenness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of enthusiasm' reads as having lost keenness, but here 'out of' means arising from it, so the phrase is an adverb meaning keenly.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting keenly, from a burning wish, is acting with zeal.

parts.note: about gives CA
L stands for a pound (from Latin libra), so two of them give LL

explanation.surface: An offer of roughly two pounds is made at auction.
explanation.walkthrough: L for pound is the £ sign's origin, Latin libra.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games such as bridge, a call is a bid.

clue.text: One is carried when you add 18 and 24

parts.note: 18 Down is ESTATE CAR, and its second word is used
24 Across is GREEN LIGHT, which means permission to go

explanation.surface: An arithmetic lesson: when adding, you carry one.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is column addition, where one is carried; the wordplay adds the cross-referenced CAR and GO.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods carried by a ship or plane are its freight.

parts.note: green means immature or not yet developed
to light is to come down or land, as a bird lights on a branch

explanation.surface: Permission is given to clear a stretch of unbuilt countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of undeveloped land' looks like greenfield countryside, but 'land' is the verb meaning settle down.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-ahead or official permission is called clearance.

indicators.note: in shows the answer sits inside these words

explanation.surface: A ghostly voice is heard in the choir.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflected sound returning without a visible source is a voice without a body.

definitions.meaning: a sport played on horseback with mallets
Marco ..., the Venetian traveller to China

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: the horseback sport with mallets, and Marco Polo the Venetian traveller.

clue.text: That's right! Olivia cooked the food

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or rearranged, so the name's letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone approves as Olivia prepares a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravioli are small pasta parcels with a filling, an Italian dish.

parts.note: a homer is a homing pigeon

explanation.surface: An impressive-looking bird is placed in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic and grand on the scale of the Iliad and Odyssey, so heroic and impressive.

indicators.note: astray means off course, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A stuffy old person led a silly companion off the path.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned, stuffy person set in their ways is a fuddy-duddy.

clue.text: Leading man embraces you religiously — he'll 1 dn

indicators.note: embraces means one word wraps around another

parts.note: a star is the leading actor in a film or play
ye is the archaic 'you' of the Bible and prayer

explanation.surface: A leading actor hugs a congregation member in a devout way.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 dn' sends you to 1 Down, SOLDIER ON: the answer is one who will carry on regardless.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse or runner with stamina who keeps going over long distances is said to persevere.
